$description: Enumeration of every interactive ImGui control in: Physics Settings, Preferences, Render Settings, Config Clipboard, Radio, Screen Recording Controls, and the Main Menu Bar. For each control: whether it has a tooltip, the tooltip text, and the file/line where it's defined.

howToRead.location: Points to the imgui.* widget call itself. For physics sliders, the tooltip text actually lives in ui/physics_params.py (the 'description' field of the parameter definition), not inline at the widget call — see sharedHelpers.

tooltipKinds.delayed: Uses _delayed_tooltip (ui/core.py:625) — only fires after the mouse hovers AND stays still (HoveredFlags_.delay_normal | HoveredFlags_.stationary). Used almost everywhere except Render Settings.
tooltipKinds.immediate: Plain `if imgui.is_item_hovered(): imgui.set_tooltip(...)` — fires as soon as the mouse enters the item. Used throughout ui/render_settings_window.py.
tooltipKinds.custom: Physics-slider-only mechanism: not a real ImGui tooltip. render_custom_tooltip() records the hovered slider's label/description, consumed once per frame by a persistent companion window (render_physics_tooltip) docked to the Physics Settings window's right edge, showing an animated shader graphic + wrapped description text. Only active for sliders with a shader mode in PARAM_BY_LABEL.
tooltipKinds.perOption: A combo/radio-group where each option/selectable has its own separate tooltip, listed as an object of option->text.

docNotes: ui/README.md is stale: it references a history_window.py/HistoryWindowMixin that no longer exists; that code is now split into ui/config_clipboard_window.py and ui/physics_tooltip.py. It also omits radio_window.py, render_settings_window.py, scheduled_renders_window.py, and generics_window.py.

sharedHelpers.name: slider_float_with_range_menu(...)
sharedHelpers.purpose: Wraps imgui.slider_float with jitter tint, right-click range/reset menu, alt-click lock.
sharedHelpers.tooltipSource: Does not show the parameter's description itself — only a fixed jitter-explainer tooltip when jitter is active. The caller (render_physics_slider) separately calls render_custom_tooltip(pdef.label, pdef.description).

sharedHelpers.name: add_slider_context_menu(...)
sharedHelpers.purpose: Right-click popup: Jitter slider, Min/Max fields, Reset Range, Reset Value buttons.
sharedHelpers.tooltipSource: Jitter slider has its own _delayed_tooltip at ui/slider_widgets.py:146. Other popup items have none.

sharedHelpers.name: render_sweep_buttons(param_name)
sharedHelpers.purpose: X/Y/C sweep-toggle buttons next to a slider (shown only when Parameter Sweeps enabled).
sharedHelpers.tooltipSource: None on any of the three buttons.

sharedHelpers.name: render_range_adjust_buttons(...)
sharedHelpers.purpose: Widen (^) / narrow (v) buttons that rescale a slider's range.
sharedHelpers.tooltipSource: One shared _delayed_tooltip at ui/slider_widgets.py:388 covering both buttons as a group.

sharedHelpers.name: render_physics_slider(pdef)
sharedHelpers.purpose: Top-level renderer used by physics_window.py for every Basics/Forces/Advanced slider; wires together lock, sweep buttons, range buttons, the slider, and the description tooltip.
sharedHelpers.tooltipSource: Passes pdef.label / pdef.description (from ui/physics_params.py) to render_custom_tooltip at ui/slider_widgets.py:447.

sharedHelpers.name: render_custom_tooltip(label, description)
sharedHelpers.purpose: Not a real ImGui tooltip — records the hovered slider/description for the physics tooltip companion window.
sharedHelpers.tooltipSource: Text = whatever description the caller passes (for physics sliders, pdef.description).

sharedHelpers.name: render_physics_tooltip()
sharedHelpers.purpose: Draws a custom borderless companion window (animated shader graphic + imgui.text_wrapped(description)) docked to the Physics Settings window's right edge. Only activates for the ~12 sliders with a shader mode in PARAM_BY_LABEL (ui/physics_tooltip.py:79-89), e.g. Global Force Mult, Strafe Power, Mutation Scale, Drag, Axial/Lateral Force.

sharedHelpers.name: _delayed_tooltip(text)
sharedHelpers.purpose: Standard hover-and-hold tooltip used almost everywhere outside Render Settings. Only shows if hover is stationary.
sharedHelpers.tooltipSource: Text passed directly by the call site.

sharedHelpers.name: inline is_item_hovered()/set_tooltip()
sharedHelpers.purpose: Render Settings' own idiom — fires immediately on hover, no delay/stationary gate.
sharedHelpers.tooltipSource: Literal string at the call site.

sharedHelpers.name: lock_widget(pls, param_name, base_label, ...)
sharedHelpers.purpose: Context manager wrapping lockable widgets (red style + alt-click toggle). Not a tooltip mechanism itself.

sharedHelpers.name: _persisted_header(label, pref_field)
sharedHelpers.purpose: Collapsing-header wrapper that persists open/closed state to preferences instead of imgui's .ini.

controls.tooltipText: Controls color variation based on particle velocity.

controls.note: alt-clickable text, not a real widget

controls.tooltipText: Determines how strongly particles respond to sensor input. Higher values make particles more reactive to the trails they sense on the Canvas.
Sets the angular offset of particle sensors from their forward direction. Determines whether particles are 'looking ahead' or 'looking behind'.
Determines distance between a particle's center and where it reads the trail information from Canvas. Longer distances tend to create larger scale patterns.
Controls the size of the random mutations applied to a rule when a new particle is clicked. At 0, every particle will behave exactly like the selected particle.
Scales axial and lateral forces applied to particles, and scales strafe power. Often tuned in the opposite direction to Sensor Gain and Drag to offset exploding/vanishing particle speed.

Each physics update, particle velocity is multiplied by drag like so:   vel = vel*drag + forces; So drag less than 1 means particles are being slowed down. Powerful (<0.5) drag values can prevent energetic systems from 'blowing up'
Controls the strength of forces applied parallel to the direction of travel: acceleration and braking
Controls the strength of forces applied perpendicular to the direction of travel: turning left and right.

Controls particle movement without applying forces to velocity. 'Strafe' is a vector added directly to position each frame, like a little hop. Strafe power scales with Axial, Lateral, and Global force multipliers.
Controls how long particle trails remain visible. Higher values create longer-lasting trails, lower values make trails fade quickly. Values close to 1.0 tend to create 'sharper' more stable patterns.
Controls how quickly particle trails spread out and blend together.
Probability per frame that particles reset to initial conditions. Gives particles a probabalistic 'lifetime' after which they reset.

tooltipText.Bounce: Particles bounce off the edges of the canvas
tooltipText.Reset: Particles are reset to their initial conditions when leaving the canvas
tooltipText.Wrap: Particles wrap seamlessly to the other side of the canvas

tooltipText.Flat Grid: Particles start in a flat grid on the floor plane, organized by cohort
tooltipText.Random: Particles are spread uniformly across the canvas
tooltipText.Ring: Particles start distributed around a circle, organized by cohort
tooltipText.3d Grid: Particles start in a 3D grid filling the volume, organized by cohort

controls.tooltipText:

each cohort has a distinct mutation.

Gravity-like force applied to particles.

Logarithmic: strafe grows ~10x per quarter of slider travel,
with a dead-zone at center.
